p: Altrincham is the kind of place where a night out naturally rolls from one spot to the next. Altrincham Market and its Market House food hall have become a big draw for local eats, making a pre-bowling bite or a post-game drink easy to sort. The town centre is compact and walkable, so you won't spend half the evening getting between places.

Getting there is simple too. Altrincham sits at the end of a Metrolink tram line into Manchester, and the interchange also has train services, which means nobody needs to draw the short straw as designated driver.

For a group booking, a little organisation saves a lot of faff. Split into teams of roughly even ability so the scores stay close, and agree a forfeit for the losers, whether that's buying the next round or doing a song in the karaoke booth. Set a time to eat, because a few frames in, hungry people get grumpy. If the group's big, two lanes next to each other keep everyone part of the same banter.

Got a morning to spare? Dunham Massey, the National Trust estate with its deer park and grand house, is just outside the town and makes for a gentle walk to clear the head the next day. It's a brilliant pairing: fresh air and deer in the morning, strikes and spares at night.
